2099. Variable Scope Within a Nested Block

80

Hard

Problem Statement
Read two integers and use them to show that a variable declared inside a nested block is separate from a variable of the same name declared in the outer scope.
Description
Read two integers into an outer variable x (declared in main) and a separate variable innerVal. Print the outer x. Then open a nested block ({ }) and, inside it, declare a new variable also named x — this inner x is a completely separate variable that exists only within the block. Assign innerVal to this inner x and print it. After the block ends, print the outer x again to confirm that it was never changed by the block-scoped variable of the same name.
input_spec: Two integers: the outer value, then the inner value, separated by a space.
output_spec: Print the outer x, then the inner x (inside the block), then the outer x again (after the block).
